categories.HEA-derived technique: HEA at f439f52 shows the technique; whether it applies to an Autobot object is a separate decision.
categories.Phase-A proposal: New in this brief or this phase; needs your decision, or is the method Phase A follows.
categories.unresolved: An open question, registered as an unknown.

verified_values.no: contradicted by the sources; see note
verified_values.n/a: a proposal, scope or method statement, not a fact to check

dispositions.PARTIALLY_ACCEPTED: Partly verified. Only the corrected form (corrected_by) may be cited.
dispositions.REJECTED: Contradicted. Kept as audit history only; never a schema rule, vector basis or decision basis.
dispositions.METHOD_ONLY: How Phase A works. Never a schema rule.
dispositions.PENDING_DECISION: A proposal waiting on a decision candidate. Never a basis until you decide it.

claims.statement: main is authoritative at 9cc0f5b, preserves cd67bfc and 09d608c, and its tree equals the verified branch tip.
claims.note: Entry chain links 1 and 2.

claims.statement: PR #1 is merged and Chapter 0's handoff, sidecar and checker prerequisites hold on main.
claims.note: Entry chain links 3 to 5; the checker ran on files rebuilt from main's blobs.

claims.statement: Chapter 0 says nothing in it is implemented; Chapters 1 to 8 implement it.
The remote topic branch and the local cleanup are bookkeeping, not architectural prerequisites.
claims.note: §6's prerequisites don't mention branches; the topic branch is still on GitHub at 09d608c.

claims.statement: Counts: 42 object types, 55 capabilities, 73 invariants, 7 state machines and paths, 6 effect types, tiers of 9, 16 and 7 fields, 5 bindings; checker 36 of 36; negative suite 11 of 11.
claims.note: There are two different sevens: 7 state machines and 7 finalization paths.

claims.statement: CLOSURE §6 scopes Chapter 1 to contracts, identifiers and canonical serialization: golden hashes for three tiers, registration and transform schemas, U-10 and U-18.
claims.note: Chapter 0 also assigns four runtime tests to Chapter 1; two of them, CH1-scope-check (INV-28) and CH1-duplicate-admission (INV-40), aren't named in the brief.

claims.statement: The ten items turn Chapter 0 into exact machine contracts without changing what it means.
claims.note: A statement of method. That Chapter 0 stays unchanged is R-2's.

claims.statement: Every object type has exactly one minter.
An architecture row such as obj-19 isn't enough to serialize, validate, store, hash, migrate or exchange one.
claims.note: objects.json has no field-level schema for any type.

claims.statement: The object classes: authority records, contracts and parts, stateful objects, receipts, journal and history, witnesses, non-authoritative records.
claims.note: The brief names 10 authority-record kinds for 8 object types (obj-03 and obj-38 each bundle two, and obj-37 has two kinds). LegacyRecord's class is legacy, not journal.

claims.statement: The inventory must separate independently versioned protocol schemas, embedded contract structures, ledger-state rows, and raw witnesses wrapped by an admission schema.
claims.note: Adopted as the schema forms in inventory.json, with append-only journal records kept apart from mutable state rows.

claims.statement: A raw Helios witness stays the producer's exact bytes; Autobot must not rewrite it and call the rewrite the source witness.
Autobot could add a WitnessAdmissionRecord (witness type, content SHA-256, producer, admission time, sequence, attempt, correlation facts).
claims.note: Not one of the 42 types. Chapter 0 references the admitted copy from the ledger and has the Collector mint the ExecutionReceipt; a new authoritative type would need a correction.

claims.statement: TaskContractRecordV1 layout: requirement, fulfillment and admission blocks plus the three digests.
claims.note: Field placement is Chapter 0's; the nesting is open. A record can't carry its own RecordHash inside the bytes that hash covers. The layout waits on dc.tier-preimages.

claims.statement: PromptProjection and WorkspaceSyncReceipt need schemas, but a parser must never let them satisfy acceptance.
claims.note: Class non_authoritative_receipt grants nothing; the enforcement is the authority_effect none in inventory.json.

claims.statement: HEA's v1 inventory listed object type, schema version, field count, schema location and implementation type, and was mechanically checkable.
An inventory record per object: class, schema required, independently versioned, canonical hash, attempt-bound, storage, minter, authority effect, runtime chapter.
claims.note: Adopted in inventory.json.

claims.statement: RequirementDigest has 9 fields, ContractDigest 16 more and RecordHash 7 more, exactly as listed.
claims.note: Checked field by field (identity.placement).

claims.statement: repository_id needs a defined syntax and equality rule.
authority_location is an enum, LOCAL or REMOTE, with different PONRs.
claims.note: The values are Chapter 0's; the wire spelling is open (U-33).

claims.statement: publication_mode is DIRECT_REF_CAS or MEDIATED; MEDIATED source finalization is blocked in v1.
finalization_class can't be prose; it enters the RequirementDigest.
claims.note: Placement is Chapter 0's, but no enum is registered; only the path names imply READ_ONLY and SOURCE_MODIFYING.

claims.statement: The fence needs a range, a start value, monotonicity, a scope, and no wraparound.
claims.note: Chapter 0 fixes what a stale fence means, not its type.

claims.statement: Identifiers such as sequence_id, attempt_id and task_contract_id shouldn't all be plain strings.
HEA corrected generic roots into typed newtypes (SemanticRoot, StorageRoot, UsageRoot, EnvelopeRoot).
claims.note: CORR-H in HEA's Phase C; the wire format was preserved.

claims.statement: Autobot should keep distinct semantic hash types (RequirementDigest, ContractDigest, CandidateReceiptHash and so on) even when the wire encoding is the same.
claims.note: The semantic types are proposed in identity_fields.json.

claims.statement: Changing reuse_policy: RequirementDigest same, ContractDigest and RecordHash different.
claims.note: Derived from the tiers by the checker (vector V-R).

claims.statement: Changing finalization_class changes all three tiers.
claims.note: V-D changes the class with requirements that fit it (coupling K-6).

claims.statement: Changing only force_new_sequence changes only the RecordHash.
resolution_path, machine paths and operational config never enter any tier.
claims.note: V-G changes the out-of-band resolution path, never a payload field.

claims.statement: Field provenance tables: field, wire type, semantic type, required, validation, tier, authority source, cross-field constraints.
claims.note: HEA's table has field, type, contract source and validation; the tier, authority source and cross-field columns are Autobot additions (identity_fields.json, couplings in vectors.json).

claims.statement: Canonical serialization is RFC 8785 JCS with SHA-256.
Pipeline: schema validation, semantic validation, canonical value preparation, JCS, UTF-8 bytes, domain-specific hash.
JCS canonicalizes syntax, not domain meaning; it keeps array order, so unordered sets need a defined sort.
claims.note: RFC 8785 sorts object members only.

claims.statement: The collections that need an ordering rule: paths, artifact paths, assertions, predecessors, capability requirements, verifier and transform registrations, floor sets.
claims.note: The list leaves out finalization_requirements and evidence_requirements, also sets, and the role_transforms and completion_policies maps. The floor is a reference whose carried assertion IDs form a collection, so it cites U-25 too. identity_fields.json lists every set- and map-shaped field.

claims.statement: Specification identity is exact bytes, never normalized through JCS; LF and CRLF versions differ unless a registered transform says otherwise.
claims.note: Not fixed: whether the bytes are the git blob or the checked-out file (U-35).

claims.statement: HEA's rules: JCS, UTF-8, duplicate keys rejected, no whitespace, defined numbers, no floats in authority fields, lowercase hex, a second JCS oracle.
Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 for every digest is still a Chapter 1 decision.
claims.note: D-09 fixes the algorithm, not the text encoding, which U-53 covers.

claims.statement: The timestamp format and precision are undecided.
Chapter 0 gives timestamps no authority ordering; version, fence, transitions and Git compare-and-swap do.
claims.note: True for audit instants such as frozen_utc, but never stated as a rule. It doesn't extend to authority windows: an expired intent, lease or delegation ends authority (INV-55, INV-60, INV-63, t-d02, which compares now with a delegation's expires_utc), so windows and the instants that end them are a separate, non-advisory question (U-39).

claims.statement: Chapter 0 fixes JCS and SHA-256 for the tiers but no typed hash construction.
Domain-separated digests with labels such as autobot/requirement/v1, the framing to be specified and tested.
claims.note: Fits inside D-09, which fixes canonicalization and algorithm, not framing; adopting it is your decision.

claims.statement: HEA had a machine-readable domain-label registry, and its hashed input bound type, version and domain.
claims.note: The registry is confirmed, but HEA's documents disagree with it on label strings and on the signature-input construction (T-25). The input that binds type, version and domain is the signature input; HEA's payload digest is a plain hash of the canonical bytes (T-20).

claims.statement: Chapter 0 doesn't require digital signatures; its authority rests on the service, the ledger and store, IPC and the presence factor.
claims.note: No Chapter 0 registry mentions signing.

claims.statement: Three kinds of hash: raw content hash, artifact closure root, semantic object identity.
Tests: the same payload in another domain gives another digest; another retry policy keeps the RequirementDigest and changes the ContractDigest.
claims.note: V-C's tier effect is specified now; V-L waits on U-28.

claims.statement: HEA pinned schema_version as an exact constant.
A v1 implementation accepts exactly v1; an authority-affecting change makes v2.
Immutable after commitment; migrations never rewrite committed bytes or keep an old hash for new bytes.
LegacyRecord is an explicit class for old v13 and v14 evidence.
Parse compatibility differs from authority compatibility: SUPPORTED_FOR_PARSE, SUPPORTED_FOR_AUTHORITY, LEGACY_READ_ONLY, UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, MALFORMED.
claims.note: HEA tested three categories (MALFORMED, UNSUPPORTED, INVALID), not these five. Since your third review the five sit in two places: parse and authority eligibility and LEGACY_READ_ONLY are compatibility policy (U-45); MALFORMED and UNSUPPORTED_VERSION are version recognition (U-31).

claims.statement: HEA used deny_unknown_fields and additionalProperties false, with no optional fields or nulls.
Autobot's authoritative objects reject unknown fields.
Use explicit variants instead of nulls, for example supersession_provenance kind NONE or SUPERSEDED_FROM.
claims.note: HEA's domain types use an enum (T-09), but its wire format keeps a zero sentinel (T-06). Tagged variants on the wire are not HEA-proved.

claims.statement: EffectIntent's outcome is the closed set PENDING, HAPPENED, ABSENT, UNKNOWN_OUTCOME.
claims.note: Chapter 0 has six states: Phase C added SUPERSEDED_BY_RETRY and HUMAN_RESOLVED.

claims.statement: External witnesses are preserved raw; an admission parser extracts what it understands, and unknown producer fields grant nothing.
claims.note: HEA's permissive mode for evidence is the same technique (T-07); the parser's behavior is open (U-41).

claims.statement: Copying HEA's 'reject all unknown fields everywhere' would be wrong.
claims.note: HEA never rejected everywhere: it was strict for signed payloads and permissive for evidence. The brief's conclusion matches what HEA actually did.

claims.statement: Chapter 0 requires golden hashes for all three tiers.
Vectors A to K.
claims.note: Tier effects are specified for B to H; A, I, J and K are blocked; none is executable yet. Phase A adds V-L to V-S.

claims.statement: HEA used two independent JCS implementations with byte-identical output and froze golden SHA-256 values.
HEA ran cross-process determinism tests.
claims.note: One test (cross_process_proof.rs).

claims.statement: The Registry's RequirementDigest must equal one the Sequencer recomputes later.
claims.note: Chapter 0 requires that Autobot compute every hash it trusts (R-4) and that the tiers be deterministic (INV-29). It does not require a second seat to recompute a Registry digest; that independent recomputation is a proposed proof (dc.test-oracles), informed by T-17.

claims.statement: TaskContractRecord binds the three digests and five freeze-time bindings.
Sequence binds the TaskContractRecordHash.
claims.note: Reservation compares state, version and record hash.

claims.statement: AttemptContract binds sequence, attempt, version, fence, source state, environment requirements and contract identity.
claims.note: Source state and the attempt identity are Chapter 0's. Chapter 0 defines an Attempt as one fenced execution against one exact source state and environment (ARCHITECTURE §1), but the environment's constraints (obj-17) live in the TaskContractRecord, and the actual environment (obj-18) is captured later as an attempt-bound receipt. Nothing in Chapter 0 puts environment requirements in the AttemptContract itself.

claims.statement: VerificationReceipt binds candidate, attempt, fence, environment, registered verifier artifacts and assertions.
claims.note: How it references assertions embedded in the contract is open (U-42).

claims.statement: CommitReceipt binds candidate, verified tree, old ref, new commit, intent, attempt and fence.
claims.note: Only for the SL canonical commit (t-s16), the point of no return, does it also carry the delegation state (INV-41) and the consumed reservation. For the REMOTE sequence ref (t-s17) it doesn't, and the verified tree holds only when the effect happened.

claims.statement: PublicationReceipt binds the reservation, repository declaration, expected old remote ref, new commit and intent.
claims.note: Missing: INV-41 freezes the delegation's state into the receipt at the point of no return, and t-s33 is one.

claims.statement: AcceptanceReceipt binds the exact finalization proof set it consumed.
claims.note: Chapter 0 requires more: the record hash, the digest, the path taken, and, for READ_ONLY contracts, the observation window. Only on RO, RUD and RUR is it the point-of-no-return receipt that carries the delegation state.

claims.statement: FulfillmentReuseReceipt binds the requester, the earlier acceptance, the same RequirementDigest, the dominance proof, freshness and EXACT_HEAD for source.
claims.note: t-s43 and t-s44 have six preconditions; the brief lists five. Missing: bindings_equal_or_policy_alternative (and the requester's reuse policy, which the brief names elsewhere).

claims.statement: DependencyReleaseReceipt binds the AcceptanceReceipt and exact DependencyEdges; a waiver satisfies no edge.
claims.note: How it references edges embedded in the contract is open (U-42).

claims.statement: Bind by immutable typed ID or hash, never by name, path, current registry lookup or HDB query.
claims.note: Binding by immutable record and hash, never by name, path or live lookup, is Chapter 0's (CORR-42, registrations.json). That identifiers are typed is a proposal (C-24, C-26, dc.identifier-model).

claims.statement: A verifier_id resolves at freeze to a registration hash and artifact root; a later registration under the same name has no effect.

The HEA techniques to carry: inventory, provenance tables, typed identifiers, exact versions, strict payloads, JCS with an oracle, golden vectors, domain binding, parity, property tests, cross-process tests, package isolation, durable unknown IDs.
claims.note: Corrected form: HEA proved these techniques (each cited with file, lines and a quoted phrase in hea_techniques.json). Whether Autobot carries each one is its own open candidate.

claims.statement: Don't copy HEA's signing, and don't reopen D-09 for digest agility.
claims.note: The digest half is Chapter 0's: D-09 fixes SHA-256. The signing half isn't: Chapter 0 doesn't require signing (C-44), but whether a record carries proof that its principal authenticated is open (U-46, dc.authentication-evidence). Listed under hea_specific_not_carried.

claims.statement: Durable unknown IDs came from an HEA Chapter 1 correction.
claims.note: CORR-F, and HEA repeated the repair in Phase C as CORR-G.

claims.statement: Chapter 0 has 18 unknowns; U-10 and U-18 enter Chapter 1.
A Python verifier needs more than its script hash: perhaps interpreter, dependency lock, OS and architecture, environment variables, tool binaries.
claims.note: Chapter 0 already fixes script plus interpreter identity plus dependency lock identity. Open: their concrete forms, and whether OS, architecture, variables and tools belong to the closure or to the captured environment.

claims.statement: HEA-style precedent suggests script SHA, interpreter identity and dependency lock identity for Python.
claims.note: That triple is Autobot's own Chapter 0 rule, not an HEA precedent; HEA's Chapter 1 has no verifier closures.

claims.statement: The content store retains the registered closure, and a missing bound artifact halts.
Phase A will expose new questions; they get new IDs and never overwrite U-10 or U-18.
claims.note: Minted as U-19 to U-55. U-39 was split from U-27, U-40 and U-41 from U-32, U-45 from U-31, U-46 from U-34, and after the independent review U-52 from U-37, U-53 from U-28 and U-54 from U-29. Each parent is NARROWED and keeps its first definition.

claims.statement: Don't assign Chapter 1 decision IDs yet.
claims.note: Candidates carry slugs only. Chapter 0 never assigned decision 15.

claims.statement: Same question keeps its ID; a different question gets a new one; a resolution keeps its history; nothing is redefined.
The ten items form one dependency chain, ending with unresolved items registered as unknowns or decisions.
Chapter 1 doesn't implement the Sequencer; it defines the language the Sequencer will use.
A genuine contradiction with Chapter 0 becomes an explicit correction with provenance, never a silent reinterpretation.
claims.note: Phase A found no contradiction, but one Chapter 0 lifecycle incompleteness: two effects require an intent that no transition creates. It is recorded as the correction candidate U-44, for you to decide, and nothing was reinterpreted. A correction is needed for a new authoritative object type, a changed minter or authority relation, a changed identity placement, or a missing lifecycle rule such as U-44's.

claims.statement: Keep HEA evidence separate: techniques HEA proved, and Autobot decisions about applying them.
claims.note: hea_techniques.json versus decision_candidates.json; the checker enforces that no candidate's basis cites HEA.

claims.statement: The entry check proves the committed chain, not just that files exist.
claims.note: Six links, all PASS.
